name: Convex polygon Minkowski sum by edge merge
definition: P⊕Q={p+q:p∈P,q∈Q}. For two CCW strictly convex polygon vertex cycles rotated to start at their lowest-y then lowest-x vertex, merge their cyclic edge vectors by increasing polar angle in [0,2π), summing co-directed vectors at equal angles. Starting at the sum of the first vertices, cumulatively add the merged edges, omitting the repeated closing vertex.
variables: P,Q closed convex planar polygons; p,q points; ⊕ set addition; edge vectors in angular order
assumptions: Positive-area simple convex inputs in CCW order with no zero-length or redundant collinear edges; exact angular ordering or robust half-plane and cross-product comparison.
limitations: O(m+n) arithmetic comparisons and output size for already valid ordered convex polygons; does not cover arbitrary nonconvex sums or input validation cost.
failure_conditions: Invalid orientation or convexity, zero-length edges, unreliable angle ties or nonfinite coordinates.
computation: Rotate input cycles to the specified starting vertices; merge edge sequences by angle, using a half-plane test then cross product, co-directed ties combined. Accumulate vectors from the summed start; check closure.

source.citation: Ron Wein et al., CGAL 6.2, 2D Minkowski Sums user manual, section Computing the Minkowski Sum of Two Polygons, text reviewed: convex edge ordering, bottommost start and linear merge. https://doc.cgal.org/6.2/Minkowski_sum_2/index.html ; tie-breaking and robust angle comparator explicitly specified here.

application: General mathematical computation on synthetic or authorised inputs; no empirical benefit claimed.
required_inputs: Two positive-area convex planar polygon boundaries in cyclic order.
incompatible_methods: Treating a mathematical specification as an implemented or validated algorithm
mechanism_note: Constructs a set sum by merging edge directions rather than testing separation or constructing a single point-set hull. Support functions add, and exposed faces in any common direction add; co-directed edges therefore combine. Opposite directions must not be treated as ties.

name: Uniform polygon area centroid
definition: For a simple polygon with cyclic vertices (x_i,y_i), let d_i=x_i y_(i+1)−x_(i+1)y_i, A=(1/2)Σ_i d_i. For A≠0 the area centroid is C=(Σ_i (x_i+x_(i+1))d_i, Σ_i (y_i+y_(i+1))d_i)/(6A).
variables: A signed area; d_i signed edge cross product; C uniform area centroid; indices cyclic.
assumptions: Simple closed finite planar polygon with nonzero area and uniform areal density; no holes in this specification; either orientation.
limitations: O(n) arithmetic; near-zero signed area and cancellation can degrade floating-point accuracy; centroid may lie outside a concave polygon and is not generally the vertex average.
failure_conditions: Zero area, self-intersection, nonfinite coordinates or unsupported nonuniform density.
computation: Accumulate signed cross products and their coordinate-weighted first moments, then divide by six times signed area. Use consistent cyclic indexing.

source.citation: Eric W. Weisstein, Polygon Centroid, MathWorld, equations (1)–(2), text reviewed: coordinate-weighted cross products divided by six times signed area. https://mathworld.wolfram.com/PolygonCentroid.html ; signed triangle first-moment derivation independently checked.

application: General mathematical computation on synthetic or authorised inputs; no empirical benefit claimed.
required_inputs: Cyclic vertices of a simple positive-area polygon with uniform density.
incompatible_methods: Treating a mathematical specification as an implemented or validated algorithm
mechanism_note: First-moment summary extends the shoelace area computation; diagnostic rather than a distinct algorithm. Signed origin-edge triangles have area d_i/2 and centroid (v_i+v_(i+1))/3, so their signed moments sum even for concave simple polygons. Reversing orientation reverses numerator and denominator together.
